Perch
A home for your coding agents.
A native Mac workspace for local and remote agent workflows.
En
glish · 简体中文 · Get started · Project status

Run Kimi or Codex on your Mac, or connect to supported agents over SSH. Perch brings
conversations,

tasks, tool output and approvals into one native workspace, so you
can read the result, inspect the
work and decide what happens next.

Built with SwiftUI, AppKit and Ghostty, with native text editing, keyboard shortcuts
and system Liqu
id Glass on macOS 26.

etails in the integrated right panel. |

## Why Perch
- **Native conversations.** Streaming replies, Markdown (including TeX math typeset natively by Swif

tMath), thinking and tool results, with details that expand when you need them.
- **Start with the r
ight context.** Choose a local or remote environment, search recent projects, and select model, reas

oning effort and permissions before sending.
- **A workspace for your tasks.** Group sessions, pin i

mportant work, archive finished conversations and return to your previous workspace.
- **Know what n
eeds you.** See running tasks, pending questions and results waiting to be read, plus Kimi's subagen
ts (including their own transcripts), background tasks with their output tails, and the session's ed

it churn (+/− per file) in the activity bar.
- **Keep your CLI workflow.** Use native chat for suppo

rted agents and Ghostty terminals for CLI sessions through Herdr.
- **Inspect the work.** Read Markd
own, source, images, PDF, tables and standalone HTML, then inspect Git changes alongside the convers

ation (experimental).
- **Keep projects moving.** Project goals and outcomes, a floating companion,
scoped search, revision-bound delivery records and one-time follow-ups. See workspace workflows for

limits and background behavior.
- **Remote execution, local control.** Files and tools run on your s

erver. Closing the Mac app leaves managed remote sessions running.
- **Explicit permission modes.**
Choose adapter-specific defaults and per-task overrides; high-risk modes require confirmation. Kimi,
Qoder and Claude Code can change for a later message or turn, while OMP and Codex are fixed when a
ode can change for a later message or turn, while OMP and Codex are fixed when a session is created.
## Agent connections
| Agent / workflow | Connection | Experience |

| Kimi Code | Kimi Web API over SSH | Native conversation |
| Oh My Pi (OMP) | RPC through the remot

e bridge | Native conversation |
| Qoder CN | Official Agent SDK through the remote bridge | Native

conversation |
| Qoder | Official Agent SDK through the remote bridge | Native conversation |
| Clau

de Code | Official Agent SDK through the remote bridge | Native conversation |
| DeepSeek Harness (d

sh) | ACP through the remote bridge | Native conversation |
| Codex | `codex app-server` JSON-RPC ov

er stdio through the remote bridge | Native conversation |
| Other CLI agents | Herdr + SSH | Termin

tdio through the remote bridge | Native conversation |
| Other CLI agents | Herdr + SSH | Terminal |

Native integrations share the same conversation UI. Additional RPC, SDK or ACP
adapters are welcome;

arbitrary protocol compatibility is not automatic.
See Kimi setup and OMP / Qoder CN / Qoder / dsh

/ Codex / Claude Code setup
for tested versions and recovery limits. Agent credentials and model con

figuration
stay with the CLI; Perch does not connect directly to model providers.

Local Kimi and Codex conversations are available; other local agents remain
discovery-only. See loca

l agents. Kimi, remote OMP and Codex support steering during a running task, with an
explicit next-t

urn option. Codex keeps its native thread ID and history, takes model
and reasoning-effort choices f

rom `model/list`, and surfaces every app-server approval
or question for an explicit response. Qoder

CN / Qoder / dsh / Claude Code support stopping and next-turn
queueing. Pending messages appear in

the conversation until runtime history confirms
them. Existing Herdr sessions remain terminal sessio

conversation until runtime history confirms
them. Existing Herdr sessions remain terminal sessions.
## Download

Grab the zipped app from Releases. The
app is ad-hoc signed (no Apple notarization): on first launch
, right-click → Open.
## Build and run

Requires macOS 26+ and a Swift toolchain with the macOS 26 SDK (Xcode 26 or newer).
The current buil

d has been tested on Apple Silicon. A remote SSH host and the
corresponding agent runtime are requir
ed for remote sessions.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

For local work, start with local Kimi or Codex setup.
For remote work, choose **Connect a remote mac

hine** on the home screen, or **Environment → +**.
The setup wizard verifies SSH, checks your chosen

agent, offers installation and
login actions, then lets you browse a remote directory and start you

r first task.
Kimi's port and token-file path are editable in Advanced settings. Fresh installs
star
t without a preset host. See the setup guide.
`⌘N` new conversation · `⌘K` search · `⌃⌥P` companion · `Return` send · `Shift Return` new line

The interface follows the system language, with 简体中文 and English available
under Settings → Language

; the sidebar and its flows are bilingual first, other
areas may still mix languages while translati

and its flows are bilingual first, other
areas may still mix languages while translations catch up.
## Status

Early source preview. Long-session responsiveness and recovery still need work;
this is not a stable
release. File previews and Git review/write workflows are experimental. Support varies by agent; ch

eck the adapter documentation before
relying on a workflow. Builds use local ad-hoc signing; notariz

ed downloads are
not available yet.
